articleTitle: Trends in RF and wireless integrated packaging: An overview
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: 1. Presentation Goals • To review and illustrate trends in Integrated Packaging for wireless and RF product designs.

articleTitle: All-inductive triplet filters with arbitrarily prescribed transmission zeros
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The paper presents all-inductive triplet filters with arbitrarily prescribed transmission zeros. A combination of TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">101</inf> and TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">102</inf> resonances in rectangular waveguide technology is used to place transmission zeros on either side of the passband of the filter. This approach has been applied to a pseudo-elliptic function filter design with a planar arranged H-plane TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">103</inf> cavity structure. Two triplets provide the generation of symmetrical located transmission zeros with respect to the passband. Verification is demonstrated by accurate coincidence of measured and computed responses.

articleTitle: Optimization of corrugated horn radiation patterns via a spline-profile
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Corrugated horns are widely used as feeds for reflector antennas [1] or as direct radiators, as in global earth illumination from a satellite [2, 3] or as source antennas in an anechoic chamber. Shaping the radiation pattern of a corrugated horn is mainly done by shaping the profile [4-6] to the required aperture dimension, and to a lesser extent, for wideband applications, by using a mode-converter [7-9] tuned to the design frequency.

articleTitle: Bandwidth enhancement of a monopole using dielectric resonator antenna loading
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A broadband monopole is investigated. The bandwidth enhancement is achieved by loading a monopole with a dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) operating in a TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01δ</inf> mode to maintain a desirable omnidirectional radiation pattern. Preliminary results validate the design concept.

articleTitle: Investigation of an octafilar helix antenna
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: An octafilar helix antenna for circular polarization (CP) is proposed and theoretically investigated. The moment method is applied to find the rigorous solutions of the current distributions on bifilar, quadrifilar and octafilar helix antennas of different helix lengths. Comparisons of calculated and available experimental results for quadrifilar helix antenna are presented, indicating good agreement. Cardioid shaped radiation pattern with excellent circular polarization over a wide angle for octafilar helix antenna is obtained. For 1/2 turn octafilar helix antenna, the axial ratio is less than 3 dB for θ ranging from −65 to 65 degrees, while the gain varies from 1.76 dB at θ=−65° to 5.34 dB at θ=0°.

articleTitle: Compact broadband transition from double-ridge waveguide to coaxial line for phased array feed
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: This paper discloses a new very broadband compact transition between double-ridge waveguide and coaxial line. The transition includes an original waveguide to coaxial mode converter and modified impedance transformer. Very good performance is predicted theoretically and confirmed experimentally over a 3:1 bandwidth.

articleTitle: A fresnel lens designed using a perforated dielectric
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A phase-compensating Fresnel lens was designed and fabricated using a flat perforated dielectric material. The perforations in the dielectric material were designed to create the zones of different dielectric constants needed to obtain proper phase compensation for the Fresnel lens. A prototype lens designed to operate at 30 GHz was fabricated, consisting of zones with four different synthesized values of dielectric constant. The lens, designed with a diameter of 15 cm, had a peak gain of 28 dB, with a 1 dB gain bandwidth of 14%.

articleTitle: Yagi-uda loops and shorted patches for a reduced size antenna
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: There is an increasing requirement to make devices smaller and at the same time interconnect them on a wireless network. One of the main challenges in the production of small wireless devices is the design of an antenna small enough to fit on the device and yet have good performance. Size reduced microstrip antenna are good candidates for this application; however, the size of the ground plane is a major impediment to its successful implementation. This paper will discuss the negative effects of reducing the size of the ground plane of a microstrip antenna and provide a unique solution to improving small antenna performance.

articleTitle: A MOM method combined with modal expansion to the analysis of dielectric resonator loaded cavities
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A new efficient method-method of moment (MOM) with modal expansion-has been developed to analyzed multilayers dielectric resonators (DR) loaded cavities. The resonant frequencies, convergence, and field distributions are presented. Also the efficiency and accuracy of this new method have been verified.

articleTitle: A novel modal analysis of circular waveguide OMT module exploiting finite plane wave series expansion
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: An orthomode transducer (OMT) is a key component in antenna feed network in frequency diversity satellite systems. An OMT can be considered as a polarization filter that separates orthogonal polarizations within the same frequency band. Two frequency channels can then be used simultaneously for enhancing system capacity. Among various OMT configurations, the waveguide junction module with circular common waveguide port and two rectangular waveguide ports for each independent orthogonal modes is frequently seen [1].

articleTitle: Some recent advances in wideband phased arrays
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Wideband phased arrays are needed to handle wideband signals and for multifunction radars. Multifunction phased array technology reduces the number of antennas needed aboard Navy ships and contributes to lower antenna radar cross section.

articleTitle: Solution bounds for some strictly diagonally dominant symmetric matrix equations
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Passive resistive circuit models are used to derive bounds for the solution of strictly diagonally dominant symmetric systems of algebraic equations with all of the off-diagonal entries being of the same sign and all diagonal and right-hand side entries being of opposite sign. The values of the unknowns are in an interval obtained from [0,1] by performing an appropriate scaling of the right-hand side entries. This bound interval indicates how to choose the initial guess for an efficient iterative solution of the systems considered.

articleTitle: A global optimization method for synthesis of multiple coupled resonator filters
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Evolutionary Programming (EP) combined with clustering technique is used as an efficient optimization method for general coupling matrix synthesis of multiple coupled resonator filters. The proposed method provides global solution when strong local minima exist in the domain of search. Examples of practical filters with general response and topology synthesized with this method are presented.

articleTitle: A new wideband closed-form green's function using 2D discrete complex images and its application in time domain analysis of a VMD over a microstrip structure
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: This paper introduces a new method of two-dimensional discrete complex images to evaluate the Sommerfeld's integral arising in the problem of a vertical magnetic dipole (VMD) over a Microstrip structure. Contrary to the conventional complex images method, which one has to find a new set of images for each new frequency, it is shown that the 2D images take into account the frequency dependence of Sommerfeld's integral, and hence the Green's function can be analytically evaluated into a simple closed-form over a wide range of frequencies. It is demonstrated that by introducing the concept of “imaginary time” and using the 2D complex images, time domain response of an arbitrary time-dependent VMD can also be represented in a closed-form. Numerical results show that both the closed-form Green's function and the time response of VMD are in good agreement with exact numerical results.

articleTitle: Design of the monoblock duplexer for repeater at IMT-2000 band
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: In the wireless communication the demand for handset is increased. A duplexer is the critical component of handset for the mobile communication to separate the transmitting and receiving signals. Thus the need of duplexer for repeater is also increased. In this paper the design and experiments for repeater's duplexer are presented. A transmission line tchebyscheff filter which will be referred as a uniform impedance resonator is presented(UIR). By using a conventional filter theory, the equivalent circuit parameters are extracted. And this paper presents simple pattern that is easy for mapping one to one with circuit components. The duplexer for IMT-2000 band is designed where Tx band is from 1920MHz to 1980MHz and Rx band is from 2110MHz to 2170MHz. A design procedure is presented and validated by simulation results.

articleTitle: Wavelets transform of the method of moments matrix arising from electromagnetic scattering from 2D objects
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: An efficient method is presented for transforming the matrix of the method of moment, which is obtained due to the expansion of the unknown surface currents with pulse basis function and the use of point match testing to a matrix with wavelet basis and testing functions. The object is 2D made of composite materials and under oblique plane wave incidence. The wavelet transform is constructed in a way to accommodate the presence of different surface current components on the object surface. The proper wavelet transform is equivalent to the use of the wavelet functions in the MoM as an expansion and testing functions.

articleTitle: A mimo measurement and demonstration system for advanced space-time signalling techniques
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: As demands on limited spectrum continue to increase, much focus is being placed on increasing spectral efficiency. One approach which has a great deal of potential in some propagation environments is to use multiple element antennas (MEAs) at the transmitter and/or receiver. Such systems have become commonly referred to as multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO).

articleTitle: Electromagnetic current and field display in classroom using em-cad tool: Zeland's ie3d
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Understanding electromagnetics and appreciating its applications in all electrical engineering studies generally require a higher level of abstraction than most other topics encountered by undergraduate and graduate electrical engineering students. The subject of electromagnetics appears insurmountable to many students and turns off their interest, especially when coupled with a lack of software tools for displaying the three-dimensional electromagnetic wave phenomena. The need to maintain student interest leads us to considering the use of simulation software and scientific visualization to render the abstract concepts of electricity and magnetism into a more intuitive form.

articleTitle: The inmarsat 4 antenna feed array
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The next generation of mobile satellite communication systems requires a high degree of flexibility. Large multibeam antennas providing hundreds of beams are used to address this need. A large deployable reflector fed by a high performance feed array provides several technical advantages and has been selected for the Inmarsat-4 program. This paper describes the Inmarsat-4 primary feed array under development at EMS Technologies. The state-of-the-art high power feed design and its main performance characteristics are presented. The challenging PIM and multipactor requirements and the unique EMS design addressing them are also discussed.

articleTitle: Simulation of potential adaptive array algorithms for 3G CDMA systems
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The goal of using adaptive arrays is to increase the Signal-to-Interference-Noise Ratio (SINR) of the communication in order to reduce error rates and to lead to better utilization of the capacity of the channel. This paper considers a number of algorithms that could be used for antenna array receivers in the mobile-to-base station link of a cellular code division multiple access (CDMA) system. Two classes of algorithms are considered: non-blind and blind adaptive beamforming algorithms. For non-blind beamforming, two solutions are presented: 1) LMS solution with training sequence, 2) Wiener solution with pilot channel on reverse link of 3G CDMA systems. For blind beamforming, we choose Least Squares De-spread Re-spread Multitarget Constant Modulus Algorithm (LS-DRMTCMA). The simulation results show the improvement of both system SINR and BER.

articleTitle: Analysis of 16-star (8,8) QAM modulation over nonlinear channels
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: This paper proposes a simple method to calculate the probability of error (POE) of 16-star (8,8) QAM constellations over nonlinear channels. The method does not need to find the decision regions for each constellation, which is often difficult to find. It does not need also any numerical calculation to evaluate integrations that appear in general when we need to calculate the exact probability of error for a general two dimensional signal constellation.

articleTitle: Cramer-Rao bound approach to super-resolution array design
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: This paper is concerned with the design of super-resolution Direction Finding (DF) arrays that satisfy prespecified Cramer-Rao Bounds (CRB) on error variance. The sensor placement problem is formulated in the framework of subspace-based DF techniques and a novel approach to the design problem, based on the concept of the CRB, is proposed. This is constructed using the prespecified performance levels that yield the sensor locations of the desired array.

articleTitle: Multi-port network modeling of multilayer planar circuits containing ground plane slots
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A new approach for Multi-Port Network Modeling (MNM) of multilayer planar circuits containing slots is introduced. Generalized network formulation for aperture problems is combined with Okoshi's model for planar circuits to obtain a unified circuit model for two planar circuits coupled through a slot of arbitrary shape in their common ground plane. The methodology, which can be easily generalized to structures having more than two layers, is clarified by applying the method to a multilayer microstrip filter.

articleTitle: Using wavelets to characterize time-frequency features of electromagnetic coupling problems
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The continuous wavelet transform (CWT) analysis is applied to electromagnetic interference data for complex topologies which have been generated by the finite difference time domain (FDTD) method. Topologies such as partially open enclosures containing conducting objects and a circuit board with different sized traces are considered. The interference source is a Gaussian pulse plane wave, covering a wide frequency band. In order to visualize the temporal variation of the frequency content of the signals coupled to the circuit board, the time-frequency characteristics of the calculated waveforms are investigated using the CWT analysis which is performed using the complex Gaussian wavelet.

articleTitle: Effect of TWT modeling error on the performance of satellite channels
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: In satellite mobile communications, TWT (Traveling Wave Tube) amplifiers are used to increase power efficiency. Unfortunately, power-efficient amplifiers cause nonlinear distortions to the transmitted signal These distortions make the received symbols no longer on the original regular lattice but on a warped one. Several authors use analytical models (such as Saleh model) to describe both amplitude (AM/AM) and phase (AM/PM) nonlinear distortions of TWT amplifiers. However there do exist some modeling error (ME) in these models (e.g. a mean squared modeling error, MSE = 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−3</sup>). Such modeling error will degrade the knowledge of the channel for the receiver, thus the receiver will become sub-optimum in the presence of modeling error. What's more, modeling error will change the decision boundaries of receiver; and therefore will decrease the detection performance.

articleTitle: Analysis of multifilar-curl antenna without ground plane
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The analysis and design of proposed quadrifilar-curl and octafilar-curl antennas without ground plane are presented. The moment method solution is used to obtain the current distribution on the antennas. The radiation characteristics like radiation pattern, polarization, axial ratio, and the antenna gain are calculated. The frequency response of the input impedance and the antenna gain are also depicted in this paper. Good polarization characteristic for octafilar-curl antenna is obtained. The octafilar-curl antenna is used as a primary feed for parabolic cylindrical reflector antennas. Grid wires approximate the parabolic cylindrical reflector surface.

articleTitle: Membrane antenna for sar satellite
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The latest generation of SAR satellites, such as RADARSAT-2, carry a large SAR payload with a mass of almost 850 kg which occupies a stowed envelope close to seven cubic meters. Antenna mass and stowed envelope are important drivers in the choice of the size of a spacecraft, as well as in the choice of a launcher. A SAR membrane antenna offers the possibility of realizing extremely lightweight, large aperture antennas having a very small stowed volume (less than 250 kg payload mass, less than one cubic meter stowed volume). This type of antenna could be implemented on a small satellite at a much lower cost. Such a SAR membrane antenna is being developed by EMS Technologies with the support of the Canadian Space Agency (CSA).

articleTitle: A reduced-complexity soft detector for iterative MIMO receivers
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: In recent years there has been much interest in wireless communication systems employing multiple antennas at both the transmit and the receive end. This class of systems, commonly referred to as multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO), has the potential of achieving remarkably high spectral efficiency in “rich” multipath environments. However, the design of practical signalling and signal processing schemes capable of supporting data rates close to the MIMO capacity limit remains a major challenge.

articleTitle: Time domain analysis of microstrip discontinuities
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Simulating high speed digital interconnect systems in time domain is of primary importance to ensure that the product meets electrical performance metrics. Circuit simulators, such as SPICE, have been developed to solve nodal equations for electrical networks and obtain currents and voltages given initial conditions and excitation sources. These simulators are also extended to handle transistor circuits. For digital circuits, simulating the output buffer stage with the transmission line interconnect system is the goal for signal integrity analysis. The signal integrity analysis aims to ensure that digital signals, modeled as analog waveforms, have good signal quality and arrive at their receiver within its allotted time window.

articleTitle: How to reduce the memory requirement of the fft t-matrix method
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The T-matrix method[1][2] has been a useful tool for studying the acoustic and electromagnetic interaction with a many-body system. One drawback, however, is the high cost of solving the resulting system of linear equations. The computational cost is proportional to N<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, solved directly and to N<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> per iteration, solved iteratively, while the memory requirement scales as N<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. Here, N is the dimension of the matrix and is often very large since it is proportional to the total volume of a scattering object. As a consequence, the O(N<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) storage scaling severely limited the technique's use to electrically small problems. Recently, the FFT T-matrix technique[3][4] was introduced to reduce the CPU-per-iteration and memory requirements to O(N log N) and O(N), respectively, making the method significantly more useful.

articleTitle: Experimental microwave radiometry prototype for medical applications
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: In this paper, we present a microwave protype of correlation radiometry destined to the medical applications. In order to evaluate experimentally the thermal inversion method, based on Kalman algorithm [1-3], an experimental prototype of correlation microwave radiometry has been setup.

articleTitle: Coplanar leaky-wave antenna with optical beam scanning control
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Next generation millimeter-wave multimedia satellites will require active antenna arrays capable of providing reconfigurable multibeam operation. The successful deployment of these systems will depend on new active array technologies capable of controlling and combining the performance of hundreds or thousands of elements. A promising approach involves the use of a periodic coplanar leaky-wave antenna structure with optically controlled phase shifters. These antennas are etched on a high resistivity silicon semiconductor substrate and are illuminated by an optical source that generates localized regions of plasma, which load the antenna structure. A dynamic antenna architecture with beam steering capabilities is realized by controlling the location of the illumination, as illustrated in Figure 1a.

articleTitle: Microstrip phase shifter using actuating ground plane membrane
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Thin film copper membranes on silicon substrates were constructed using micromachining techniques. Membranes were used as flexible ground planes beneath a microstrip transmission line. Actuation of membranes induced phase shift in the transmitted signal. Membranes possessed radial surface corrugations 10 μm deep to increase their flexibility. Membranes were released using a combination of KOH and XeF2 backside etching. Surface corrugations were made using KOH etching on the frontside of the wafer. Membrane flexibility was studied as a function of diameter and corrugation pitch. A phase shift of 30.03° at 12.08 GHz was achieved by actuating an array of five 4 mm diameter membranes beneath a microstrip line.

articleTitle: Application of MEMS technology to rf/microwave systems
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: It can be said that the field of MEMS was originated by the late Richard P. Feynman back in 1959 when he made the observation “there is plenty of room at the bottom.” [1]. Feynman reached this conclusion upon conducting a special type of search, namely, a search for a boundless field. He noticed that fields like endeavoring to attain low temperatures, or attaining high pressures, had virtually no end in sight. That is, you could never say/claim you had reached the lowest temperature or the highest pressure. His search led him to discover a new field, namely, that of miniaturization, whose goal was to engage in a program to make everything small. Wondering why had so little been done on miniaturization, Feynman determined that, while there were no innate limitations imposed by the laws of physics, these were actually rooted in technology, that is, it is our ability to make small things that sets a limit on miniaturization. Having acknowledged that miniaturization was limited by technology, and that this limitation would erode in time, Feynman went on to consider what if the technological problem/limitation was nonexistent? How would miniaturization impact three particular areas of application, namely, Information Storage, Computers, and more pertinent to this presentation, Machines?

articleTitle: Circularly polarized reflectarray using microstrip dipoles
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A novel approach for generating a circularly polarized microstrip reflectarray with variable size rectangular microstrip elements is presented. The concept was implemented with a linear feed-horn illuminating microstrip dipoles which are arranged in a non-overlapping perpendicular configuration in the lower Ka-band (20 GHz) and as crosses (overlapping dipoles) in the upper Ka-band (30 GHz). Experimental results indicated that the perpendicular CP array had a peak efficiency of 31.2% with a 3 dB Axial Ratio bandwidth of 6%. In addition, we observed that both LP and CP could be achieved by simply changing the orientation of the feed-horn with respect to the reflectarray elements.

articleTitle: Wideband single — polarised finite array of vivaldi antenna
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: This paper describes a finite difference time domain analysis to design a broadband Array in 12–18 GHZ frequncy band with beamwidth of 30 degree and minimum SLL of −13 dB. The effect of diffraction due to finite ground planes, variation in phase velocity, frequency-dependent impedence, interaction between elements and detailed field structures is taken into account. The current distribution, coupling between elements, radiation pattern are calculated. The computed radiation pattern results of the vivaldi antenna array agree very well with experimental results.

articleTitle: Circular patch antenna with a circular arc slot and an L-probe feeding
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Recently, extensive research has been devoted to the bandwidth enhancement of microstrip antennas. Several techniques such as the use of thick substrates [1], and the use of multiple resonators [2, 3] have been reported. Earlier, it has been shown that a bandwidth of 30% can be achieved by introducing a U-shaped slot on the microstrip patch [4], and a bandwidth of 24% can be obtained by using an L-probe on a thick substrate circular patch [5]. Later on, another broadband antenna was presented in which both the U-slot and L-probe techniques were used with a circular patch [6]. This antenna has an impedance bandwidth of 38% and a gain of 6.8 dBi with good radiation pattern characteristics.

articleTitle: Macro and micro diversity schemes for the W-CDMA system employing smart antennae®
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The macro- and micro-diversity schemes for the W-CDMA base stations deployed with smart antennae are investigated and their performances in terms of the improvement in the received bit energy to interference PSD ratio are evaluated, where both the adaptive and fixed beam schemes are considered for smart antenna systems. The macro-diversity scheme is employed to compensate the decrease of antenna gain when mobiles are located in the overlapping areas between two adjacent beams, while the micro-diversity is employed to collect the multipath signals in the directions other than the mobile's direction. A multipath collecting algorithm is proposed to perform micro-diversity, and associate simulations are performed to evaluate its' performance.

articleTitle: A new antenna implemented in laminated waveguide
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The requirement for greater bandwidth in military satellite communication systems has resulted in research for systems that can be used in the EHF band. To support this requirement, the Department of National Defence has sponsored the development of unique Canadian technology under the CANMILSATCOM project that is part of the Canadian commitment to the US Advanced EHF Satcom (AEHF) project. The end goal is to provide the Canadian Military with worldwide military satellite communications to support Canadian Forces operations.

articleTitle: Virtual path optimization in satellite atm networks with stochastic traffic flows
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: In Satellite ATM (SATM) networks, the various traffic patterns and dynamically changing topology call for effective network traffic control mechanisms to reduce congestion and utilize network resource efficiently. There are two major challenges in the SATM traffic control. On one hand, the time varying traffic arises big challenges for guaranteed service in ATM. On the other hand, due to the permanent mobility of the entire LEO satellite network, the network traffic control task requires highly sophisticated approaches to provide the predominant connection-oriented services with acceptable QoS for the end users and efficient use of network resources.

articleTitle: Effect of a ground plane perforation on far-field phase
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A unit cell comprised of a circular aperture is modelled centered in the ground plane beneath a microstrip patch. A phase change of 82–86° is obtained at the patch resonant frequency in the far-field for a cell radius of 0.4L, where L is the resonant length of the patch. A stacked patch structure is investigated to maintain an adequate match at the resonant frequency of the unloaded patch. A phase change of 127° is reported with the stacked patch for a cell radius of 0.2L.

articleTitle: Radiation pattern enhancement of microstrip patch antennas using a 2D photonic band gap structure
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Recently, there has been extensive research on the photonic band gap structures (PBG's) and their applications in the microstrip antennas and transmission lines. The PBG structures have the unique property of preventing the propagation of EM waves in certain directions for certain frequencies. The properties of these structures are defined by the shape, size, symmetry and, the constituent material. These periodic structures come in many shapes and forms. Some of these include drilled holes in the dielectric, patterns etched in the ground plane, and metallic patches placed around microstrip structures. The PBG structure studied in this paper consists of metallic patches with center vias connecting the patches to the ground plane. The properties of this 2D structure are studied using the Ansoft Ensemble simulator which is based on the method of moments (MOM). Two microstrip patch antenna using the PBG structure are designed and the effects of the PBG on the gain and radiation pattern are shown. It is observed that the radiation pattern of the patch antennas can be controlled by changing the parameters of the surrounding PBG structure.

articleTitle: Investigation of the coupling to a wire inside a box with apertures by means of FDTD simulations
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The induced current in a wire placed inside a conducting box due to field penetration through apertures has been studied using FDTD simulations. Two box configurations have been investigated in order to evaluate the difference in coupling with one large aperture and the combination of a large and a narrow aperture. The coupling to a wire placed above a ground plane has also been studied to compare it with the test cases involving the box.

articleTitle: Modal analysis and design of the dual-band orthomode junction
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: An analysis and design concept for the dual-band orthomode junction is presented. The centerpiece of the design is a waveguide six-port cross junction. Its modal analysis is verified by measurements available in the literature. After introducing appropriate symmetry planes for the orthomode junction, a principal design approach is outlined. The entire procedure is demonstrated for a K/Ka-band design example. The final design is compared to results from the commercial software package HFSS and is found to be in good agreement.

articleTitle: Efficient transient simulation of networks containing lossy frequency-dependent interconnects
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Since the introduction of the Asymptotic Waveform Evaluation algorithm [1], model order reduction techniques have shown high computational efficiency for fast solution of large interconnect problems. The reduced-order models of linear interconnect networks can be derived by matching network moments via Padé approximations. For interconnect networks containing distributed transmission lines, the associated moments can be generated by using the eigenvalue moment method [2] or the matrix exponential method [3]. In the former method, the moments are generated by computing eigenvalues and eigenvectors of the transmission line propagation matrix. It is noticed, however, that the accuracy of the moments calculated by using the eigenvalue moment method decreases with the increase of moment order due to the truncation error in evaluation of the eigenvalues and eigenvectors. Accurate generation of moments is critical in applying moment matching techniques to interconnect analysis since small errors in the moments can considerably affect the accuracy of the simulation results. In order to obtain more accurate transmission line moments, one can apply the matrix exponential method. In this method, the moments are obtained by expanding the transmission line parameter matrix as a Taylor series. The moments of transmission lines with frequency-dependent parameters can be computed in the same manner [4]. Although the matrix exponential method can generate more accurate moments, it is computationally more costly than the eigenvalue moment method due to the slow convergence of the matrix exponential series.

articleTitle: Novel adaptation technique for web browsing using satellite networks
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Mobile web browsing is becoming very popular with the recent advances in the satellite and wireless networks, and the growing popularity of the World Wide Web. The mobile users generally have limited resources, such as low bandwidth and low-resolution terminal, compared to the conventional desktop users. It is important to develop techniques that will enable the mobile users to access the web efficiently through a low bandwidth wireless network by using their low-resolution terminals with limited memory. In this paper we propose a dynamic adaptation technique to enable the efficient and fast access to the web documents for users with handheld mobile devices such as satellite or cellular phones.

articleTitle: Beam focusing properties of a circular monopole array on finite ground plane
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Wire monopole antennas are widely used for wireless mobile communication systems, because of broadband characteristics and simple fabrication method [1-2]. In multipath terrestrial propagation environment, sector beam needs narrow beamwidth with good horizontal gain, so that while switching the beams from sector to sector, least interference between sectors is present [3]. One way to generate the narrow beam is to excite one element of the circular array (Figure 1), while the other elements are kept passive behaving as reflector [4]. This is similar to the corner reflectors, where by adjusting the aperture angle beamwidth and directivity can be controlled [3]. This paper presents the study on beam focusing properties of a circular monopole array on finite ground plane size by exciting more than one monopole element at a time in a six element circular array capable of generating six sector beams. The effect of varying the number of monopole elements in the array, while exciting only one element is discussed, as well. By placing a reflector behind the array further improves the beam focusing performance. For this study, a circular ground plane of radius R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</inf>=1.50λ=30 cm is selected. The design frequency for this study is 1.50 GHz. The simulations are carried out using Finite Element Method (FEM) program, Ansoft's HFSS [5].

articleTitle: Serially concatenated systems using MSK modulation
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: In this paper, Serial Concatenated Convolutional Code (SCCC) with Continuous Phase Modulation (focus on MSK) and Log-MAP decoding algorithm is investigated. As an alternative solution to Parallel Concatenated Convolutional Code (PCCC), which is termed Turbo Code (TC), SCCC is in some cases superior to that of TC with similar complexity, especially at high Signal-to-Noise ratio. SCCC consists of a Recursive Systematic Code (RSC) or non-RSC outer code and a RSC inner code permuted by a random interleaver.

articleTitle: Millimeter-wave monolithic balanced bpsk modulator using overlay coupler
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: An overlay structure broadband CPW coupler has been realized at millimeter-wave frequency and the size is only one third of the Lange coupler with same performance. It was used to construct a BPSK modulator employing balanced reflection topology with HBTs acting as switches. The modulator showed ±0.2dB amplitude imbalance and ±2° phase error over 26.5∼30.5GHz.

articleTitle: Design and implementation of three-dimensional block turbo codes
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: This paper investigates multi-dimensional Block Turbo Codes (BTCs) with trellis-based decoding, which have the possibility of providing a large range of block sizes. Large block size codes can provide significant coding gain and code rates. BTCs thus provide us more attractive options for a wide range of applications and higher bandwidth efficiency. Due to their excellent power and bandwidth efficiency, BTCs can be applied to many data packet systems such as ATM and MPEG.

articleTitle: The antenna design software
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Antenna design starts with a desired electrical performance, stating the minimum gain, beamwidth and/or other parameters, across a specified bandwidth. An antenna type is chosen, and then trial-and-error is used to choose the dimensions, usually in conjunction with computer simulation. This paper introduces an antenna design tool called the Antenna Design Software (ADS) which accepts the desired electrical performance as the input, and determines all the possible combinations of geometrical dimensions that meet this performance for a given antenna type. There may be many such sets of dimensions, or conversely there may be no set of dimensions that meets the required performance. The ADS can be used to study any antenna system that can be designed with two primary geometrical parameters, and is based on a database of antenna performance constructed using any computer simulation program. This paper introduces the software's basic functionality using a simple cylindrical helix operating above an infinite ground plane.

articleTitle: C-band direct digital receiver MMIC
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A new direct conversion and high speed uni-mode (QPSK) receiver designed with MMICs is proposed for 5.8 GHz ISM-band communications. The receiver architecture consists of one MMIC module for receiver front-end to include a six-port based circuit with matched RF detectors and low noise amplifiers (LNAs). A second module of receiver is designed with hybrid integrated circuits (HIC) and it performs all base-band functions including amplification of output signals from the six-port, carrier recovery and I-Q decoder circuit. The maximum bit rate (at least 50 Mbps) is determined solely by analog circuitry and the limit is directly related to the sensitivity of signal level comparators. The receiver designed with MMIC module is proposed as a low cost robust receiver for high data-rates applications. Simulation results are presented for MMIC prototype and measurements are given for equivalent HICs.

articleTitle: X to k-band 0.18 μm CMOS amplifiers
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Complementary metal oxide semiconductor (CMOS) processes are beginning to be used at frequencies traditionally restricted to more expensive gallium arsenide (GaAs) and indium phosphide (InP) processes. The lower electron mobility and significant substrate conducance makes silicon an inferior microwave substrate compared to GaAs and InP, but offer high levels of integration with digital processing circuits and lower cost. Amplification is a fundamental system requirement, and so the design of narrowband and broadband amplifiers in CMOS will be examined here.

articleTitle: Spectrally efficient non-binary turbo codes: Beyond DVB-RCS standard
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: While the DVB-RCS standard turbo code, which uses quaternary alphabet and QPSK modulation, has an excellent performance, its bandwidth efficiency is limited by the puncturing and QPSK modulation to less than 2bits/s/Hz. In order to achieve bandwidth efficiencies of 2bits/s/Hz and higher, one needs coding and modulation schemes with M-ary alphabet (M>4). We have investigated an extended non-binary turbo-coding scheme consisting of 8-ary (triple-binary) codes combined with 8PSK modulation to increase the bandwidth efficiency. A comprehensive study over AWGN channel is carried out to show the good performance of the concatenated codes, the influence of various parameters and the symbol-by-symbol Max-Log-MAP algorithm. The novel triple-binary code still has the features of circular recursive systematic convolutional (CRSC) codes, which avoid the degradation of the spectral efficiency. The circulation state and the different permutations (interleaving) are also discussed. The subject of this project is the design of nonbinary turbo codes, that is, how to choose and/or design the components in a turbo encoder to get the best possible performance and higher transmission rate. However, since turbo codes are decoded using an iterative suboptimal decoding algorithm, new design criteria arise. In fact, the success of iterative decoding proves to be related to the choice of the component codes in the turbo code encoder and the modulation scheme used. Triple-binary CRSC codes inherit most of the advantages of double-binary CRSC codes, however, they are more flexible and efficient for encoding blocks of data. Especially, the 8-ary alphabet of triple-binary turbo codes, when combined with 8PSK and puncturing, makes it possible to achieve high code rate and more than 2bits/s/Hz bandwidth efficiency while double-binary CRSC code and QPSK modulation cannot exceed this restriction. An interleaver operating on a group of bits replaces the bitwise interleaver known from classical binary turbo codes, and the equations of permutation parameters are chosen similar to the interleaver of DVB/RCS turbo codes. The structure of the iterative decoder and the symbol-by-symbol Max-Log-MAP algorithm are derived for non-binary trellises to avoid numerical problems and to reduce the decoding complexity. The study of 8-ary triple-binary CRSC codes show their potential as an alternative for more bandwidth efficient transmission of data via satellites. Triple-binary CRSC codes with 8PSK modulation give excellent performance at 2bits/s/hz. This is bandwidth efficiency not available by double-binary CRSC codes in DVB-RCS standard.

articleTitle: Internal probing of mm-wave integrated circuits
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: There is currently no instrument capable of providing internal vector-voltage measurements of mm-wave integrated circuits. We present a non-contacting probe capable of non-invasive internal amplitude and phase measurement of high-frequency MMICs. Accurate and localized voltage measurements can be made without complex calibration and without depassivation of test points. A probe with a >26 GHz bandwidth, <10 fF loading, <10 mV amplitude and <2° phase resolution, and a μm spatial resolution is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Low profile array for broadband aeronautical satellite data links
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Airframe manufacturers, avionics companies, satellite operators and major airlines have launched programs to develop high speed data services for use on commercial aircraft and business jets. Inmarsat currently supplies aircraft with medium-rate data service and high quality voice throughout the world on both spot-beams and global beams. In 2001 EMS Technologies began installing Inmarsat BGAN transceivers on military and commercial aircraft. These terminals provide full-duplex communications at 64KBPS per channel with two channels offered in the standard configuration. With the launch of Inmarsat 4 satellites the data rates achievable with the BGAN service will be increased substantially. Programs, such as Connexion-By-Boeing however aim to leapfrog this capability with data rates of several MBPS being proposed.

articleTitle: MEMS tunable inductor
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: This paper presents the implementation of a MEMS tunable inductor using admittance J-inverters and a variable capacitor. The tunable inductor circuit consists of two inductors, two fixed capacitors and a variable capacitor. The MEMS tunable inductor has been fabricated using the CRONOS MUMPs® Process. Design details and results are presented for a tunable inductor designed to operate over a bandwidth of 1 GHz at L-band.

articleTitle: A circularly polarized, low profile loop antenna with a wide radiation pattern
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: It is known that a loop antenna of one wavelength circumference radiates a linearly polarized wave in the direction normal to the antenna plane. It is also known that, when perturbation elements are added to the loop, the linearly polarized wave can be changed to a circularly polarized wave [1]. For mobile communications, the circularly polarized wave at low elevation angles is often required to have a certain field strength. One way of meeting such a requirement is to widen the radiation beam.

articleTitle: A combined transmit/receive feed system for personal mobile communications in l/s-band in consideration of increased power applications
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A strong increase in the demand for regional GEO based mobile communication services is expected during the next decade. Since the GEO systems operate in L- or S-band, they require reflectors with diameters typically ranging between 12 and 15 m and a corresponding feed system of more than 100 radiating elements. With respect to accommodation and mass one combined transmit / receive (Tx/Rx) antenna is preferred rather than two separate transmit and receive antennas. Another advantage of the combined antenna is the congruence between up- and downlink beams considering the narrow footprints of the beams (typical: 0.6° to 0.8°), this is an important issue.

articleTitle: Space multibeam antenna with very high G/T, for ka-band multimedia via satellite missions
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A typical multimedia via satellite mission needs to cover, from a geostationary orbit, a large terrestrial zone with 40 to 50 semi-contiguous beams, for very high gain & re-using 10 to 12 times the same frequency resource, by dividing the available bandwidth in 4 sub-bands, 1 spot-beam over 4. Such multibeam antenna much increases the System capacity, for providing broadband services directly to users at home or office, wherever in the world. We point out the Focal Array Fed Reflector as the most suited receive-antenna architecture, for various kinds of coverages, to provide high figure of merit (G/T) and inter-beams isolation. A demonstrator has being built under the IST/ MultiKaRa contract, co-funded by the European Union. We present the design and performances of the whole antenna, especially the highly integrated “active receiving feeds”, and explain how a cold thermal control of the active focal array improves the antenna G/T by 1 dB, allowing cheaper User terminals (20% less power to be transmitted).

articleTitle: A spatial decomposition technique for large phased arrays using region overlap
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The full-wave analysis of large-scale phased array systems poses a very challenging computational electromagnetic problem. Conventional full-wave techniques such as the Method of Moments (MoM) can handle small-to medium-scale problems relatively easily. When the size of the array exceeds a hundred elements, full-wave techniques reach their limit of applicability. For larger arrays, periodic simulators are often utilized, whereby the array is assumed to have an infinite extent. However, periodic techniques cannot predict the edge effects due to the radiating elements located at the boundary of the finite-size array structure. Therefore, it is essential to develop a technique that utilizes the full-wave analysis of the array in an efficient manner while being able to recognize the finite size of the array and account for the edge effects.

articleTitle: Endfire- and backfire-mode helical antennas
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A helix whose arm is composed of a uniform section and a tapered section, referred to as a UT helix, has been analyzed using the method of moments [1]. The analysis shows that the tapered section contributes to the reduction of the reverse current traveling toward the feed point. This reduction generates a radiation beam with almost purely circular polarization. It has also been revealed that the size of the ground plane backing the helical arm affects the beam direction [2]. Detailed analysis shows that, as the size of the ground plane decreases, the backward radiation increases.

articleTitle: Low-cost focusing element for milimeter-wave monopulse radar
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A focusing system based on low-cost foam printed technology is investigated. The design is based on artificial lenses which consist in stacked parallel-plate waveguides of various lengths. The foam technology allows a single block configuration with the primary source. As the dimensions of the lens are at least 10 λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>, full-wave analysis is not appropriate for fast design. A theoretical model [1] based on ray tracing, Goudet's formula and array factor is used, compared with electromagnetic models and validated by the experiment. Various lens configurations will be investigated and presented to meet collision avoidance radar antenna specifications.

articleTitle: Radio frequency specific absorption rate inside a human body due to a manpack radio
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: In this work, Radio Frequency (RF) electromagnetic (EM) energy coupled into a human body model carrying a Manpack radio is investigated using the finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method. A human body model consisting of twenty-three tissue groups is used to accurately represent the human body anatomy. The Specific Absorption Rate (SAR) and conduction current magnitudes are calculated for the cases of the body model standing on dry and 13.77% wet loamy soil conditions at frequencies of 20, 30, 60, 80, 100, and 150MHz. This investigation shows that more EM radiated energy is coupled to the lower part of the body model than to the upper region at 20 and 30MHz, while more energy is coupled to the upper region at 100 and 150MHz. The wet loamy soil case resulted in higher SAR and conduction current values in the foot region as compared to the dry loamy soil case. However, no significant change is observed in the upper body region for both loamy soil cases considered.

articleTitle: Nonredundant NF-FF transformation by a bi-polar scanning facility
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Measurement techniques in the antenna near-field (NF) region play a significant role in the evaluation of far-field (FF) patterns. In fact, for electrically large antennas, the required size of the conventional FF range becomes prohibitively large. Moreover, the development and the spreading of NF-FF transformation techniques employing planar, cylindrical or spherical scanning systems is justified from the fact that each approach has its own particular advantages, depending on the antenna under test (AUT) and the measurement requirements. Last but not the least, NF facilities provide a controlled and secure environment, and all weather capability. Among the NF-FF transformation techniques, that employing the plane-polar scanning has attracted considerable attention due to its particular characteristics [1]. In such a scanning the antenna rotates while the probe travels in a linear motion, so that the NF data are acquired in concentric rings centered on the AUT. The large computer time, required in the earliest approach [1] to reconstruct the far-field, has been drastically reduced by recovering the plane-rectangular data from the plane-polar ones, thus enabling the use of FFT [2]. In [3], by exploiting the quasi-bandlimitation properties of electromagnetic (EM) fields [4], an optimal sampling interpolation (OSI) algorithm has been developed to recover the plane-rectangular data from the plane-polar ones. It minimizes the truncation error and is stable with respect to errors affecting the data. Moreover, at variance of the previous approaches [1, 2], the number of samples for each ring stays bounded even if the ring radius goes toward infinity and, on increasing the measurement plane distance, the radial step can be significantly larger than that previously adopted. However, when the radius of the scanning zone approaches infinity, the overall number of samples becomes unbounded. This shortcoming has been overcome in [5, 6], where field representations over a plane from a nonredundant number of samples, which stays finite also for an unbounded scanning plane, have been developed. They have been obtained by considering proper geometrical modellings of AUT and by exploiting the results [7] concerning the nonredundant representations of the EM fields radiated by sources enclosed in arbitrary convex domains with rotational symmetry and observed on surfaces having the same symmetry. The bi-polar scanning proposed by Rahmat-Samii et alii in [8, 9] represents a convenient alternative to collect NF data over a plane. In such a scanning the AUT rotates axially, whereas the probe is attached to the end of an arm which rotates around an axis parallel to the AUT one. This allows to collect the NF data on a grid consisting of concentric rings and radial arcs (see Fig. 1). The bi-polar scanning maintains all the advantages of the plane-polar one while providing a simple and cost-effective measurement system. In fact, since the arm is fixed at only one point and the probe is attached at its end, the bending is constant and this allows to maintain the planarity. Moreover, rotational movements are preferable to the linear ones, since rotating tables are more accurate than linear positioners.

articleTitle: Measurement of scan element pattern of wideband arrays
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Scan Element Pattern, SEP, (formerly active element pattern<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>) was developed circa 1960 by Allen [1], Oliner [2], Hannan [3], Stark [4], and others, to provide phased array gain behavior versus scan angles. It's utility for decades has been to give insight and results on the scan performance of various elements and lattices. A common measurement procedure terminates all elements in the array, with the excited center element connected to a gain measurement setup. As early as the Lincoln Lab reports [1] it was recognized that the impedance seen in the measurement procedure was not the Scan Impedance (SI), (impedance seen when all elements are excited with the proper amplitude and phase), due to the passive mutual couplings. In Allen's derivation the textbook definition of gain was used; Scan Impedance mismatch was not included. Hannan did include mismatch, but his formulas were based on “intuitive reasoning”. Clearly his SEP proportional to cos θ is only approximate; it fails for large scan angles. Allen derives SEP for the center element excited case under the assumption that the isolated element pattern is equal to the element pattern in the array with all elements terminated. With this assumption it can be shown that transmit SEP (single element excited) equals receive SEP, with impedance determined in both cases with all elements excited. For single mode elements such as dipoles this assumption is very good; almost nothing will affect the shape of current on a thin dipole. However for more complex elements the element pattern with other elements terminated is not equal to the isolated element pattern.

articleTitle: Smart antenna simulation environment in ADS®
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: An end-to-end smart antenna simulation environment has been created in the Advanced Design System (ADS®) from Agilent Technologies. Because ADS® is able to co-simulate with various other design tools, system implementation becomes much faster. Although a full-blown RF level simulation is possible, the run-time of the simulation is extremely slow. To improve the speed of the simulation, a base-band version of the antenna array model as well as the beamformer has been created and simulated in ADS®. Because of the faster run-time, the base-band simulation could be used for testing and analyzing the performance of the adaptive algorithm.

articleTitle: The linear tapered slot antenna as a holographic antenna feed
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A linear tapered slot antenna (LTSA) is investigated as a novel feed mechanism for holographic antennas. This new slotline feed is low profile and compact in comparison to traditional holographic antenna feeds such as open waveguides and horns. Measured results indicate that the LTSA is an efficient and viable feed for holographic antennas.

articleTitle: Radar cross section of a large rectangular cavity with a partial floor
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: In this paper we develop a model for the RCS of an open ended rectangular cavity with a partial floor, as in Fig. 1. The purpose is to gain further understanding of the RCS of aircraft cockpit-like structures. This is an extension of previous work for a PEC floor cavity in the sidewall of a finite cylinder [1].

articleTitle: Measured performance of a ultra broadband dual polarized scanned array of ridge elements
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The measured performance of a dual polarized array of ridge elements arranged in a square egg-crate lattice is presented. The array is designed to operate over a 4:1 frequency band (4.5–18 GHz), within a conical scan range of ± 22.5° and with a scanned VSWR less than 2. The test results show that these electrical characteristics have been achieved without any resonances or deep dropouts. Further, the cross-polar isolation is better than 20 dB within the scan coverage in all planes and is thus superior to the commonly used Vivaldi and Bunny Ear printed elements.

articleTitle: Temperature dependance of the mechanical properties of an RF MEMS switch
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: In the Institute for Microstructural Sciences we have been developing a surface micromachining process for the fabrication RF MEMS on quartz substrates. In a previous paper we reported on the microwave performance of these switches [1]. In this paper we report on the characterization of the switch mechanical properties as a function of temperature. Real world electronic devices must meet a minimum of 0°C to 70°C operation range. Many devices must work in the range of −40°C to 85°C such as portable devices like hand phones. Since we are developing a relatively unique process, we do not have a reference that indicates how our MEMS device will behave as a function of temperature. Since the device uses silicon nitride for the main suspension and the substrate is quartz, we expect to find temperature dependent stress due to difference in expansion coefficient. We have also found that the metals used for the electrostatic actuator may change properties with low temperature 50°C annealing. Hence we are concerned with the possibility of hysteretic behaviour. We focus on the mechanical stiffness or spring constant. This is a key parameter in determining the actuation voltage. Any changes in this parameter would be an indicator of a long term reliability problem. We are testing our devices in the temperature range 10°C–80°C using the apparatus shown in Figure 1.

articleTitle: On radiation pattern measurements of circularly-polarized antennas using dual-linear probes
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: This paper revisits aspects surrounding the measurement of circularly-polarized (CP) antennas with dual-linearly-polarized probes. Two experimental setups are considered and polarization conversion expressions given for each. A probe calibration procedure is also presented and discussed. Measured results that illustrate the effectiveness and possible shortcomings of this procedure are given. The methods presented here are not new; however, some of the details gained from experimentation were not found to be explicitly stated elsewhere in the literature.

articleTitle: Single axis and dual axis bow-tie antennas
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: This paper will present the design and development of a single axis and a dual axis bow-tie antenna. For the single axis bow-tie antenna, a dual band performance is obtained with its maximum bandwidth of 22.8%. For the dual axis bow-tie antenna, good circular polarisation with axial ratio of less than 2dB is obtained from 1.4GHz to 2GHz. Improved methods to feed both antennas will be shown.

articleTitle: Comparison of RADARSAT-1 and RADARSAT-2 SAR antenna design and capabilities
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The paper summarizes the technical features of the RADARSAT-1 and RADARSAT-2 SAR antennas. Key antenna performance requirements are reviewed. Antenna architectures are briefly described Different antenna subsystems are compared in terms of the technology used.

articleTitle: Radio-localization of rovers on mars
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The Space Robotics Group at the CSA is currently working on the design of small rovers for Mars' exploration. These small vehicles will be able to cover large distances from their landing site and will require some kind of localization system.

articleTitle: V-slot microstrip antennas for wideband applications
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The rectangular microstrip patch antenna with V shape slot is presented in this paper (Fig. 1). With this new configuration 33.5% impedance bandwidth with stable radiation pattern is achieved.

articleTitle: Multiple beams antenna by RF delay line beam-forming network
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: In this paper the RF delay line is used as the beam-forming network to generate eight beams for giving antenna array aperture. There are eight beam patterns from the eight antenna elements in this MBA (Multiple Beams Antenna) system. The eight antenna elements are the coaxial collinear antennas with quarter wavelength above the ground plane. The beamwidth for these eight beams are changing from 10° to 15° with in the 70° azimuth sector coverage. The test results of the performances in this MBA are agreed with that of the simulations.

articleTitle: Path models and mimo capacity for measured indoor channels at 5.8 GHz
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Cumulative distribution functions (CDFs) for multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) capacities are computed for flat-fading indoor channels at 5.8 GHz. These CDFs are based on two measured channels and on reconstructions of the MIMO channels from path parameters that are estimated based on measured data. The measured data was obtained using the stepped-frequency method of channel sounding in combination with 3-D virtual arrays (also known as synthetic arrays) at both ends of the link. The channels were measured for various antenna element spacings. Several versions of the ESPRIT approach are used to estimate the complex amplitudes, delays, directions-of-arrival (DOAs) and directions-of-departure (DODs) of each path of propagation. One version sequentially estimates each set of parameters. Another version estimates the delays and then jointly estimates the DOAs and DODs, and still other versions jointly estimate all the parameters. A residual estimation error (REE) approach to detecting the number of paths is proposed. We compare the REE results and the capacity CDFs for the different parameter estimation methods and for different antenna element spacings. Sensitivity of the capacity to spacing is observed.

articleTitle: Compact range techniques for RCS and antennas ANTEM 2002, Montreal, Canada
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: (This paper is an adjunct to the seminar talk to be presented at the ANTEM 2002 Meeting on August 1, 2002 in Montreal, Canada. The talk will have many more visual aids and discuss some other special topics.)

articleTitle: Electrodeposition of multilayer cantilevers for MEMS applications
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: An automated electrodeposition process has been developed to produce low-stress freestanding metallic cantilevers for rf MEMS applications. The cantilevers are made of multiple layers of three different materials to achieve stress compensations. The fabrication is carried out using a PC-controlled deposition system developed in house. We found that the deposition rate increases with the increase of applied voltages and the thickness of the films has a linear relationship with the deposition time for individual layers. The deposited multilayer films have a smooth surface and are uniform in thickness. The morphology of the films is independent on the thickness of the multilayer films when a moderate deposition rate is adopted. Cantilevers with a single sandwich structure are fabricated and studied. All of the samples have demonstrated freestanding cantilevers with a uniform thickness and smooth surfaces. However, a slightly up bending (or sloping) along the cantilever is observed on all cantilevers regardless the big difference in thickness (ranging from 1.5 μm to 5 μm), which indicates the presence of some uncompensated stress. Cantilevers with a double sandwich structure (with two strengthening material) are also fabricated to further reduce the stress. The relative thickness of the individual layers for the three materials is found to govern the stress compensation process and to control the quality of the cantilevers. The strengthening layer not only plays an active role in stress compensation, it also hardens the multilayer films and to cut down the required minimum thickness for the cantilevers. The optimized deposition conditions produce essentially flat cantilevers with a length up to 800 μm. For each sample, the two cantilevers are found to be identical in shape, thickness and morphology.

articleTitle: Evaluation of the coupling coefficient between patches in stacked patches using a new radiation model
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Stacked patches have many performances [1] that make them the most appropriate option for many applications due to their wide band and easy manufacturing. However they are not many systematicways to design such antennas. This work presents a new radiation model for such antennas. The model is based on the two-slot radiation model for simple patches, and consists of a four or six element array depending on the supposition of infinite ground plane. Several useful parameters can be extracted from this model. This work will be centered in one of them: the coupling coefficient between upper and lower patches. This coupling coefficient will be a new tool in design of such antennas.

articleTitle: Circuit modeling of unsymmetric matrix equations
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: General unsymmetric systems of linear algebraic equations are modeled by linear electric circuits using a procedure previously developed for symmetric systems [1]. Augmented symmetric systems are constructed from the original unsymmetric ones and then the modeling technique based on the node-voltage method is applied. The unknowns of a system of equations are simply obtained by measuring the nodal electric potentials on its model.

articleTitle: Application of single source surface integral equations to transverse electric scattering by a lossy dielectric
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Formulations of electromagnetic wave scattering by lossy dielectric bodies in terms of volume integral equations require a large amount of computation due to the volume distribution of unknown sources and some of them are unreliable when applied to dielectric bodies with large values of relative permittivity. The analysis of wave scattering by coupled surface integral equations reduces the dimensionality of the problem by employing unknown sources only distributed over the surface of the dielectric bodies. Two unknown surface current densities are used in these equations. Wave scattering by lossless homogeneous dielectrics has also been modeled quantitatively by using only a single unknown surface current distribution instead of the two distributions of electric and magnetic surface currents in the classical coupled surface integral equations, thus reducing by half the number of unknowns required. The integral equation satisfied by the density of this surface current is the so-called single source surface integral equation (SSSIE) [1]-[3].

articleTitle: Microstrip antennas with reduced surface-wave and lateral-wave excitation
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Surface-wave and lateral-wave excitation from microstrip antennas results in undesirable edge diffraction of these fields from the edges of the substrate and ground plane, as well as undesirable mutual coupling between antenna elements. The edge diffraction of the surface waves and lateral waves may result in significant degradation of the radiation pattern, including frontside pattern rippling and backside fields. The mutual coupling due to the surface waves and lateral waves causes variations in the array scan impedance, including effects such as scan blindness.

articleTitle: Pcb inductor and capacitor in antennas design for automobile communication at uhf
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: It has been common practice for several decades to fit private cars and commercial vehicles (such as taxi, police car) with radios or two-way communication devices. The mobile antenna for cars has been widely studied and somehow mature, such as whip antenna, invert-L antenna and loop antenna [1], [2], [3].

articleTitle: Design and qualification test results of large deployable reflector for ets-8
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: NEC TOSHIBA Space Systems, Ltd. (NTSpace) has been developing the Large Deployable Reflector (LDR) for the Engineering Test Satellite-8 (ETS-8) under contract from National space Development Agency of Japan(NASDA). The design of LDR has been certified through the qualification tests, the element tests and the several kind of analysis. And critical design review (CDR) was performed and closed with fruitful conclusions in this February. Now we are preparing for manufactures of two sets of LDR flight models, one is for the data transmission and the other is for the reception. We could advance in knowledge and technology concerning such the large deployable reflector through ETS-8 project activities. This paper presents the representative results of the designs and the qualification tests concerning LDR.

articleTitle: Feed chain design for the W3A Ka-band antenna
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The paper presents the design concept and bread board test results of the feed chain for Eutelsat W3A Ka-band antenna. The design of the feed chain components was carried out by systematic synthesis, analysis, and optimization techniques using advanced full wave design tools. The predicted and measured results are in good agreement.

articleTitle: Design of a 44.5 GHz yagi-like antenna on ltcc material
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
