abstract: Low temperature co-fired ceramic (LTCC) is a multilayer material used for system packaging. It offers many advantages in high density integration for RF to millimetre-wave integrated circuits [1]. It is therefore an attractive technology for packaging phased array modules, where the size is an important issue especially at millimetre-wave frequencies [2]. The circuits realised with other processes, such as GaAs MMICs (monolithic microwave integrated circuits), are assembled in a multilayer configuration using printed lines and vias. The antenna elements of the phased array are then built flush with the LTCC material, lowering losses, assembling complexity and, therefore, cost.

articleTitle: An integrated sp3t rf MEMS switch
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: In this paper, a novel multi-port MEMS switch is investigated. The switch is integrated on a chip of size 500μm × 500μm, while maintaining a high isolation between all ports up to 40 GHz. Electromagnetic (EM) simulation results are presented to verify the proposed concept. The switch is fabricated using the Multi-user MEMS processes MUMPs for integration on an Alumina substrate using flip-chip technology.

articleTitle: Resonant frequencies of triangular microstrip resonators using novel formulation for effective side length
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: In this paper, a novel factor is used to cater for fringing field effect in triangular resonators. This factor is valid for both equilateral (symmetric) and non-equilateral (non-symmetric) triangular resonators. The problem of obtaining the resonant modes of the resonator is solved using the finite element method. Finally, the procedure is used to obtain the resonant frequencies of shapes other than equilateral triangular resonators namely: equilateral triangular resonator with curved vertices for different curvature ratios and isosceles triangular resonators.

articleTitle: Scattering from a small chiral radome of arbitrary shape
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A simple moment method technique is used to compute the scattering cross section of a small chiral radome of arbitrary shape. Numerical results are presented for a spherical shell and a cube radome. The computed and exact results for the spherical shell are in good agreement.

articleTitle: Modelling of shielding effect of a fence on the performance of a Yagi antenna
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: This paper concerns the effect of a metal fence on the near and far fields of a Yagi antenna. We use a moment method implementation of the electric field integral equation for our computations. The presence of the fence generally lowers the field intensity in the near shadow region of the fence. However, in the far field, the presence of the fence can, depending on the geometry, in fact raise the field intensity. The fence's influence on the fields depend upon a number of factors including antenna frequency, distance between the antenna and the metal fence, observation angle, and the height and width of the fence and its inclination to the ground. The effect of these parameters on the antenna performance is investigated. Some recommendations are made for the optimum use of metal fences as shields.

articleTitle: Design of a small size microstrip antenna proximately coupled to a hook shape probe
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Personal mobile communications requires small size and lightweight antennas with wideband performance. Also, multi-bands antennas are needed. The design of such antennas was based on ad hoc experimental investigations. With the advancement in numerical method and its accuracy with ease of its use in the analysis of complex structures, many new small antennas are designed [1-2]. Microstrip antennas are widely used in these applications because of its lightweight. It is well known that bandwidth of the microstrip antenna patch can be increased by increasing the dielectric substrate thickness and using dielectric substrate with low dielectric constant. If the microstrip patch is excited by a coaxial probe (central conductor electrically connected to the patch), when the thickness exceeds about 0.05λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">˚</inf>, the lead inductance prevents the direct matching of the antenna to the widely used 50ω transmission lines. Therefore, wideband small microstrip antennas are developed based on thick air filled substrates and modifications for the probe shape [2] or using a U-slot on the patch [3]. To have efficient coupling between the proximity coupling probe with the patch an L-shaped probe is used and proved to be an efficient excitation mechanism that achieves wide matching frequency band. The same excitation mechanism has been used with different microstrip patch geometries [4]. To further reduce the patch antenna size, the patch that is excited by modes that has null electric field at its middle is cut to half the size and short the patch from one end to the ground plane. This will almost keep the same operating frequency band, but the radiation patterns become different from that of the full size patch because the shorted patch radiates only from one edge. It is also known that increasing the width of the radiating edge increases the rectangular patch bandwidth.

articleTitle: Penalty function based 2D adaptive digital beamforming for satellite communications
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Two dimentional (2D) adaptive digital beamforming is one of the promising smart antenna technologies to meet the rapidly increasing demands for more capacity of satellite communication systems. However, the conventional 2D adaptive digital beamforming algorithms have the jitter and high sidelobe problems especially when the number of antenna elements is large. In this paper, a penalty function based 2D adaptive digital beamforming algorithm is proposed to estimate the weights of 2D antenna array. A penalty function is added to the original minimum square error (MSE) function. The formulas of estimating the weights are derived using the modified MSE function. System capacity and signal-to interference ratio (SIR) of the new 2D adaptive digital beamforming algorithm for satellite communications are also analyzed. Experimental results show that the penalty function based 2D adaptive beamforming algorithm can overcome the jitter and high sidelobe problems of the conventional adaptive algorithms. Compared with the fixed beam approach, the adaptive beamforming method has higher system capacity and SIR with the tradeoff of higher computation load.

articleTitle: Dielectric resonator filter design exploiting space mapping optimization
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: In this paper we exploit the space mapping optimization technique [1] to design dielectric resonator filters. The coarse model is a network model consisting of a coupling matrix and input/output transmission lines. The fine model is simulated by Ansoft HFSS. The idea is to establish a mapping between the filter design parameters and the coupling elements. This mapping is approximated by a linear relation and is updated iteratively until reaching the optimal design. The technique is very efficient and converges to the optimal design in a few iterations. We illustrate the design technique through a 4 pole dielectric filter design.

articleTitle: Tapering an incident plane wave
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: This paper presents a technique for generating an amplitude tapered incident plane wave of a prescribed polarization and a prescribed incidence angle by summing a finite number of propagating uniform plane waves each constitutive plane wave having is own propagation direction, its own amplitude and it own polarization. The choice of the propagating plane waves corresponds here to a sampling of the physical angular space (θ,φ). This contrasts with the 2-D Fourier transform technique of Reference [1] that corresponds to a sampling of the spectral plane (κ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>, κ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">y</inf>) where κ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> = sin(θ) cos(φ) and κ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">y</inf> = sin(θ) sin(φ). Our technique is based on the summation of propagating plane waves only whereas the technique of Reference [1] is based on the summation of both propagating and evanescent plane waves. Evanescent plane waves are plane waves with Imag(κ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">z</inf>) ≠ 0 and correspond to points of the (κ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>, κ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">y</inf>) plane lying outside the unit circle of the spectral plane. The dominant plane wave is the plane wave with its propagation direct corresponding to the prescribed incidence angle described by the spherical angles θ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</sup> and φ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</sup>. Both techniques are vector forms of the scalar theorem of plane wave spectrum decomposition. The motivation for producing a tapered beam here is to avoid the diffraction waves caused by illuminating also the edges of a scatterer of which we want to compute by FDTD simulation the reflection and he transmission coefficients corresponding to the bulk material property of the scatterer.

articleTitle: TM Scattering by a chiral elliptic cylinder
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: This paper presents an eigenfunction solution for a transverse magnetic (TM) normal incident plane wave on a chiral elliptic cylinder. The solution is expressed in terms of vector wave functions with unknown expansion coefficients. The coefficients are determined by matching continuity of the tangential components of electric and magnetic fields at the chiral elliptic cylinder surface.

articleTitle: Assessment of minimal-separation criteria in a 50-m corridor
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: In a hospital, portable radio frequency (RF) sources can cause field strengths in excess of immunity levels of some critical-care medical devices, unless appropriate minimal separations are maintained between sources and devices. This paper examines the risk of medical-device interference due to a 1900 MHz cell phone transmitting near one end of a 50-m hospital corridor. Detailed maps of corridor field strength are calculated, using geometrical optics, in planar cross-sections at various heights above the floor. For a device of given immunity, the interference risk is quantified from the ratio: (number of locations with immunity exceeded)/(total number of locations). Minimal-separation distances (separations ensuring that transmitter fields fall below a given device's immunity level) obtained assuming free-space propagation are compared to minimal separations specified in the current IEC standard for medical electromagnetic compatibility (EMC). It is concluded that using the separations of this standard effectively reduces the interference risk to zero.

articleTitle: The atacama large millimeter array (ALMA) a next generation radio telescope
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: We describe in general terms the main characteristics of a new, very large Radio Telescope for the (sub)millimeter wavelength region. It is an aperture synthesis array telescope consisting of 64 individual reflector antennas of 12 m diameter, which are interconnected to form 2016 simultaneous two-element interferometers. The total collecting area is more than 7000 m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and the angular resolution will be variable from ∼10 arcseconds to ∼10 milliarcseconds. The telescope covers the entire frequency range from 30–950 GHz with 10 separate receiver units. To minimize atmospheric effects, it will be located at 5000 m altitude in Northern Chile. The project is a collaboration between North America (USA and Canada) and Europe with the likely later participation of Japan. After several years of development, the project is now entering the construction phase. Completion is scheduled for 2011.

articleTitle: Parallel-plate method for creating electric fields from 1 MHz to 1000 MHz
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A unique means of generating low-to-medium, radio-frequency voltages with triangular parallel plates is presented. The method is novel due the wideband (1 MHz to 1000 MHz) nature of the parallel-plate device. A current application is the immunity evaluation of electronic units with dimensions less than 1m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. Unit dimensions and metal mass are the limitations of the method. Performance comparisons with a square and a fractal approximation demonstrate the viability of this technique.

articleTitle: Efficient backward motion compensation based scalable wavelet video coding for satellite channels
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Digital video communication is becoming popular with the recent advances in the satellite and wireless networks, and the growing popularity of the World Wide Web. The mobile users generally have limited bandwidth, and hence it is crucial to develop efficient scalable video coding scheme for low bandwidth channels. The current video coding standards are primarily based on discrete cosine transform (DCT). However, efficient wavelet-based coding schemes are being investigated in the last few years.

articleTitle: A parallel processing scheme for high-speed implementation of turbo codes
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: An important characteristic of turbo codes is the iterative nature of their decoder. One of the factors in determining the performance of turbo decoder is the number of iterations that is used for decoding each input sequence (frame). Using more iterations means decoding more sequences correctly. For example a decoder with 6 iterations per frame is not capable of decoding sequences that may be corrected in 7, 8 or more iterations. On the other hand, in practice, increasing the number of iterations increases the decoding delay, hence, reducing the decoder throughput. So, we have turbo decoders with limited capability and fixed number of iterations. This project proposes a parallel processing scheme to increase the performance and/or the throughput of turbo decoders.

articleTitle: Microstrip ring resonator using slow wave structure exhibiting harmonic suppression
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: This paper presents a microstrip ring resonator design which exhibits suppressed harmonic excitation and high quality factor. The resonator is constructed from four quarter-wave coupled-line couplers, connected in a square configuration. Of interest is the change in the frequency response of the ring when corrugated couplers are used in place of ordinary couplers. By direct comparison it is shown that the use of corrugated couplers in the construction of the ring results in an increase in quality factor from 34 to 47, and 30 dB rejection of the first harmonic, at the expense of a 1.5 dB increase in insertion loss and a reduction in harmonic frequency from 2.858 GHz to 2.701 GHz.

articleTitle: Smart antennas configurations for dual polarization and dual frequency systems
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Smart antennas take advantage of both antenna and propagation technologies. It has the potential to reduce multipath interference, increase signal to noise ratio, and introduce frequency reuse within a confined environment. Several challenges remain however in the development of smart antennas and one of these is the availability of efficient radiating elements interfacing with the beamformer. This study was focused on the design of a novel antenna topologies planning its use as building block for deploying smart antenna systems that could offer range extension, improved immunity to flat fading, interference suppression and Spatial Division Multiple Access. The proposed antenna configurations are able to demonstrate broad bandwidth characteristics, compactness, and polarization/frequency diversities with CPW feed lines, and have been proven to work well. The effectiveness of this antenna has been experimentally confirmed.

articleTitle: Implementation of the DVB-RCS turbo codes
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: In this project, the hardware implementation of double-binary CRSC codes in the Digital Video Broadcasting (DVB) for the Return Channel via Satellite (DVB-RCS) is investigated for use in satellite communication links. The simplified Max_Log_MAP algorithm is derived for the Non-binary convolutional turbo code, which follows the specifications of turbo coding/decoding in the DVB standard, for twelve different block sizes and seven coding rates, and the simulation results for AWGN channel show the performance of this coding scheme. The correction coefficient of the simplified Max_Log_MAP algorithm is discussed and considered in the simulation results. Moreover, an optimized 4-bit quantizer for in put data is designed for this turbo. The simulation results are very close to the unquantized results with a reasonable and good tradeoff between implementation complexity and decoding performance. The transformation from floating to fixed-point is done with the goal of performing the hardware implementations of the turbo code. The hardware implementation of DVB/RCS decoder presented in this project is designed according to the above mentioned algorithm. The design architecture is implemented in Very high speed integrated circuit Hardware Description Language (VHDL) and synthesized on a single chip FPGA (Xilinx Virtex-E). This hardware design adopts hierarchy, regularity, modularity and locality strategies. It is optimized in both speed and area by using parallel, pipeline and algorithm optimization. With Synopsys tools the RTL level simulation has been carried out. The results prove that the decoder works at a speed as high as 20 M bps (for Virtex II 200MHz) and 6 Mbps (for Virtex E 60 MHz).

articleTitle: Two level beam MEMS variable capacitor and its charactarization
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A novel MEMS variable capacitor having two level suspended beams is proposed. The addition of another beam considerably extends the maximum possible displacement, which in turn increases the capacitor tuning range. The tuning was simulated using CoventorWare and found to be 670%. The achievable tuning range far exceeds that of traditional MEMS variable capacitors of the same type. The proposed MEMS variable capacitor is built using the MUMPs process.

articleTitle: Complexity evaluation of sova based algorithms for decoding of block codes on a sectionalized trellis
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Turbo decoders are composed of two or more soft-input soft-output (SISO) decoders that exchange reliability information. A classical way of implementing a SISO decoder for a linear block code is to use a trellis-based decoding algorithm, such as MAP, Max-Log-MAP or SOVA [1]. Recently, the idea of sectionalizing the trellis diagram representing a code has been proposed as a means to decrease the decoding complexity associated with the SISO decoders [2-3]. In this paper, we investigate the application of a nonbinary SOVA decoding algorithm to the sectionalized trellis of a binary linear block code. Considering an (n, k) block code C, a minimal bit-level trellis has n sections. A ν-section sectionalized trellis with section boundaries U = {0, h<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>,…, h<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">v</inf> = n} is obtained from the bit-level trellis by removing any stage at a location not in U, and connecting the remaining states by branches whose labels are the labels of the paths originally connecting the nodes in the bit-level trellis (Our notations borrow from [1], so the reader is referred to this book for further details). Optimal sectionalization boundaries can be chosen in order to minimize the complexity in terms of operations and/or memory of a given algorithm for a particular code (such optimal sectionalizations have been derived for MAP [3], Max-Log-MAP [3] and Viterbi [2] decoding).

articleTitle: FPGA Implementation of RM-BTC Codec using Log-MAP Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Turbo Codes have been an attractive topic in coding theory community since they were introduced in 1993 due to their powerful error correcting capability and superior coding gain. Thanks to their astounding performance, Turbo codes are used in 3rd generation wireless communication and satellite communication system. Fore these applications, efficient implementation of Turbo Codes, i.e., development of codecs providing high throughput with low power consumption and small chip area are of growing importance.

articleTitle: Generalized knowledge-based neural network for microwave modeling
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: This paper presents a general method combining microwave empirical/equivalent model with artificial neural networks for efficient modeling of microwave components. The method, called Generalized Knowledge-Based Neural Network (GKBNN), unifies several existing methods and provides increased model accuracy and extrapolation capability, even if the training data is limited. It is applied to microwave device and transmission line modeling for high frequency/high speed circuit design.

articleTitle: Phased array implementation using ground plane reconfiguration
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Phased array antennas are presented, where the array beam is scanned by changing the effective phase delay of its feed network and resonant frequency of its elements, in lieu of using external phase shifters. Sample preliminary methods, based on MicroElectroMechanical (MEM) elements, for effecting the phase delay changes are proposed and discussed.

articleTitle: Parametric study of PBG ground planes in microstrip transmission lines
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Photonic bandgap structures (PBG) are periodic structures in 1, 2, or 3 dimensions which, can prevent the propagation of electromagnetic waves in certain directions for certain frequencies [1]. The properties of these structures are defined by their type of symmetry, material, and by the shape and period of the structure. These periodic structures can be drilled through the dielectric or etched in the ground plane. Etching of holes in the ground plane makes the design much simpler to fabricate. It has been shown that by etching circular holes in the ground plane of a transmission line, a filter can be created with a stopband that is a function of the period of the holes [2]. In this paper, the properties of PBG ground planes in microstrip transmission lines is studied in detail. The effective epsilon values are calculated and compared with simulated values. Finally, a new PBG filter with a wide stopband is shown along with the measurement results.

articleTitle: Defining an effective point of radiation for a microstrip patch antenna
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: In many high-precision GPS applications, accuracies on the cm level are required. However, due to the nature of GPS measurements, the signal transmitted by the satellite traverses the ionosphere and troposphere, along a different path for each incident (observation) angle, before it is detected by the receiving antenna on earth. Thus, in addition to the delay the GPS signal experiences associated with the path length between the satellite and the receiver, the signal also undergoes an additional timing delay due to the complicated nature of the propagation medium [1]. While the effects of these delays (phase errors) are typically minimized by using differential GPS techniques [1], an additional timing delay that is often neglected is associated with the variation in the antenna's effective point of radiation (“phase center”) as a function of the observation angle. Even with differential correction of the ionospheric and tropospheric phase errors, the timing delay associated with the phase center variation can degrade the positional accuracy of precision GPS measurements. Hence, a thorough characterization of the effective point of radiation for a GPS antenna is important.

articleTitle: Analysis of a printed quadrifilar helical antenna with the fdtd method
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: In recent years, the printed quadrifilar helical antenna (PQHA) has become an attractive candidate for use in mobile communication systems due to its features of circular polarization, good axial ratio and mainly its low cost.

articleTitle: Microstrip antenna array using photonic bandgap substrate
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Photonic Bandgap (PBG) structures have been successfully applied to antenna design in order to raise the antenna radiation efficiency. In application of PBG structure in microstrip antennas design, mainly two techniques are used. One is to introduce a periodic lattice in the substrate layer. The seemingly simplest way to achieve this is to drill a periodic lattice of holes on the substrate slab. It is reported that for a single microstrip patch antenna, the radiation efficiency, backlobe and endfire radiation have been greatly improved by using a PBG substrate of drilled holes over the conventional bulk substrate [1]. It has also been revealed that PBG structures improve the antenna performance by suppressing the propagation of surface waves. This has been experimentally verified by measuring the mutual coupling between two distant microstrip antenna elements built on PBG substrate [1], or superstrate [2]. An alternative approach is focused on construction of a planar periodic lattice of metallic patch array on top of a dielectric substrate layer, and similar improvement was observed [3, 4]. By appropriately design of the element geometry and the lattice constant, an equivalent perfect magnetic conductive (PMC) surface was achieved over a limited band of frequency. Such a PMC surface can be applied in antenna design to suppress the flow of surface electric currents, which is the major source of edge diffraction, therefore improves the radiation property of the antenna.

articleTitle: An application of CMA circular array for CDMA systems
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: In this paper, we apply the Adaptive Antenna Circular Array (UCA) with Constant Modulus Algorithm (CMA) at the base station of a CDMA mobile communication system. The BER performance of CMA algorithm in such system is simulated in AWGN channel, Rayleigh Flat Fading channel, Frequency Selective Fading channel with angle spread and carrier phase error.

articleTitle: Investigation of the performance of a reflectarray fed by an active feed block to establish link with ACTS
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The performance of a dual band reflectarray fed by an active feed block is investigated by evaluating Tx/Rx link with NASA's Advanced Communications Technology Satellite (ACTS). The reflectarray antenna has two focal points, one for the lower Rx band (20GHz) and one for the higher TX (30GHz) band. An array of active patches was developed for the higher Tx band and a cavity backed antenna was developed to feed the antenna in the lower Rx band to increase the power handling of the antenna system and meet the link budget requirements. The issues related to the performance of the feeds were carefully studied. The link budget was derived and is presented in the paper.

articleTitle: Ground plane PBGs and their effects on the performance of microstrip patch antennas
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Microstrip antennas are known for their advantages in lightweight, low volume, low cost, and compatibility with integrated circuits. These advantages make this antenna a useful candidate in applications such as mobile radio, satellite communications, biomedical radiators and feed elements for reflectors. An important factor in the performance of microstrip patch antennas is the ground plane. The size of the ground plane has a significant effect on the radiation pattern and the gain of the patch antenna as reported by S. Noghanian and L. Shafai [1]. In addition to the size of the ground plane, it has been shown that by etching holes in the ground plane one can control the excitation of certain modes of a microstrip patch antenna [2]. In this paper, the effects of perforations in the ground plane on the performance of narrow band and wide band patch antennas are studied. It is shown that by placing a hole or multiple holes in the ground plane of a simple patch, one can cause a shift in the resonance and an increase in the bandwidth of the antenna. In addition, placing slots in the ground plane of a narrowband microstrip can create a frequency shift of the higher modes and in the case of a wide band antenna an increase in the bandwidth.

articleTitle: Integrated waveguide technology — An attractive approach for point-to-multipoint transceiver equipment
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Integration of a passive microwave subsystem and equipment housing is shown to improve performance as well as facilitating large scale and low cost production requirements for a digital point-to-multipoint (MDMS) terminal equipment. Particular design constraints — yielding several novel component designs, as e.g. cavity filters with improved stop band performance, single acting strip line to waveguide transitions — are discussed in detail. Investigations respecting manufacturing tolerances and environmental conditions are presented. The approach is realized in a 10 GHz MDMS terminal equipment. Since there is no possibility for measuring the passive subsystem or components thereof during manufacturing, the designs have been verified experimentally by representative hardware prior to the series production.

articleTitle: New adaptive polynomial and neural network predistortion techniques for satellite transmissions
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: In order to allow maximum exploitation of the frequency spectrum, the current trend is to increase the spectrum efficiency by using high modulation techniques e.g. multilevel quadrature amplitude modulation (QAM). The use of High Power Amplifiers (HPA), e.g., TWT, in satellite communications channels causes severe nonlinear distortions to the transmitted signal. The transmitted signal is more sensitive to these nonlinear distortions when the number of symbols in the signal constellation increases. The effect of the HPA can be sufficiently reduced by backing-off the output signal levels from the amplifier's saturation point. However, this reduces the transmitted signal power and consequently the power efficiency. Therefore, there is a tradeoff between power efficiency and spectral efficiency. Nonlinear distortions of the HPA give rise to some unwanted effects such as, warping of the signal constellation. Also, nonlinear characteristics of the TWT cause an increase of the Adjacent Channel Interference (ACI) due to widening of the transmitted signal spectrum.

articleTitle: Modeling and simulation of wave propgation in graded-index waveguides and optical couplers
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: This paper uses the Beam Propagation Method (BPM) to develop a Matlab-based toolbox with a user-friendly graphical interface for modeling and simulation of guided wave propagation in graded-index waveguides and optical couplers. Matlab has been used to develop the toolbox since it has powerful graphical features that allow for the propagation patterns to be interactively displayed along the waveguide structure. Using the developed simulation toolbox one can understand and visualize the wave propagation phenomena in graded-index waveguides and optical couplers.

articleTitle: Slow-wave characteristic of EBG structure and its use for a phase shifter
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The slow-wave propagation along novel 1-D electromagnetic bandgap (EBG) structures for finite-width conductor-backed coplanar waveguides is investigated. By controlling the pattern and size of the perforation and the length of EBG cell, this structure exhibits different slow-wave and stopband characteristics. A series of these cells appears as a slow-wave transmission line that can exhibit larger phase shift.

articleTitle: A novel green's function analysis of microstripline structures with finite substrate
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A novel technique to derive a closed-form Green's function for finite dielectric structures is introduced using the Characteristic Green's Function (CGF) and the complex images techniques. As an example, a closed-form Green's function of the scalar potential for a finite 2-D dielectric substrate on an infinite ground plane is derived. Characteristic impedance of a microstripline on such a substrate is calculated by employing this Green's function in the method of moment (MOM) formulation. Numerical results show good agreements with other numerical techniques.

articleTitle: Ray optical simulations of UWB through-wall radar imaging
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: This paper demonstrates the suitability of ray optics in conjunction with the Huygen's principle for EM simulations of UWB through-wall radar imaging. In the proposed scheme, targets are represented by their Huygen's equivalent currents, and walls are modeled by using a dielectric flat-plate formulation. The geometrical optics (GO) method is used to account for both the incidence and the multiple reflections of RF propagations in the indoor environment. The ultra-wideband propagation is simulated in the frequency domain using a large number of frequency points. An inverse DFT is implemented to compute range profiles of the receivers. 2D radar images of the surveyed area are constructed using back projection.

articleTitle: Quasi-optical measurement system for material characterisation
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: In most MMIC and antenna applications, an accurate knowledge of the relative permittivity of materials is required. At EHF, the two-port transmission/reflection quasi-optical measurement system is an attractive solution due to its contactless and non-destructive nature and to the simplicity of sample preparation. The quasi-optical apparatus consists of a pair of collinear horn-fed lenses. The sample to be tested is inserted midway between the two lenses. The horn-fed lenses create a Gaussian plane wave at the sample location, which allows plane wave theory to be used in the calculations. Figure 1 shows a representation of the measurement system.

articleTitle: A comparison of three methods for the loss characterisation of microstrip lines printed on heraeus ct2000 ltcc from 20 to 40 GHz
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Estimating the attenuation constant of a low loss transmission medium is by no means a simple task at microwave and millimetre wave frequencies. In this paper, the attenuation constant of microstrip line printed on Heraeus CT2000 LTCC [1] is determined over the 20 to 40 GHz range using three different analysis techniques. All three methods yield different loss estimates, which begs the question as to which method should be considered the most accurate. Although the ultimate aim of this work is the loss characterisation of the microstrip, it also provides an opportunity to explore the issues related to accurate loss evaluation.

articleTitle: Silicon micromachined ka-band cavities with planar line feeds for use in future generation broadband satellite communications
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A micromachining technique involving the wet chemical etching of bulk silicon wafers has been used to fabricate deep three-dimensional cavity resonators at 30 GHz. Previous attempts at forming cavities using silicon micromachining have been inhibited by the shallow depth of the cavities, which were on the order of a single wafer thickness (∼0.5 mm). This seriously degrades the available unloaded Q-factor (Q<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>) of the cavity, which is proportional to the total cavity volume. In addition, there are added contact resistances and air-gaps due to the bonding of the wafers that are unavoidable for these cavity designs. In contrast, our technique has tried to address these issues, by introducing a two-sided etching process that allows for much deeper cavities, thus increasing the available Q<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>. This procedure also makes the alignment of the etched wafer sections much easier, which was another obstacle of past research efforts. Most importantly though, this process allows the cavity structure to be metallized after the wafers are stacked together to form the 3-dimensional shape. This enables the air-gaps and contact resistances, which appear after the wafer bonding, to be covered up and therefore their effects are reduced.

articleTitle: A 24 GHz scanning receiver array
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: A 24 GHz scanning receiver array is presented based on a frequency scan of the LO signal fed to the array mixers. To allow a wide scan with a reasonably low LO frequency variation, sufficiently long delay lines are employed between the coupling points for the separate mixers. Losses are kept low due to a standard metal waveguide network which later on may be replaced by waveguides fabricated by plastic injection molding. Scan range is nearly 50° with a LO frequency variation from 19.35 GHz to 19.8 GHz.

articleTitle: A small-pitch helical antenna operating in conical mode
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The antenna characteristics of helices for the normal and axial modes [1] have been theoretically revealed using numerical techniques. However, little theoretical analysis has been performed for revealing the antenna characteristics of the conical mode [2][3]. With this background, this paper presents the antenna characteristics of the conical mode helix. The antenna characteristics presented here are obtained using an electric field integral equation [4] solved using the method of moments [5].

articleTitle: Broadband CPW quadrature overlay coupler
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: In this paper, the design and measurement of a 3dB broadband coplanar quadrature coupler are discussed. An overlay structure for the quadrature couplers is proposed to reduce the size, realize 3dB coupling and broaden bandwidth. A coupler with overlay material ∊<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf>=4 was fabricated and the measured results showed a bandwidth of 20GHz. The area is only one-third that of the Lange coupler with similar performance.

articleTitle: Methods to reduce memory requirements in turbo decoding
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Since the introduction of turbo codes in 1993, researchers have turned their attention to the design, performance evaluation and practical application of these codes. The practical implementation of turbo decoding algorithms faces two major challenges: (1) heavy computations for the α and the β values, and (2) huge memory requirement. Using powerful fast processors, which are in hand nowadays, one can somehow compensate the former. However, incorporating a large amount of memory in the practical turbo code devices is still a problem. Hence, it is desirable to find methods to reduce the memory requirement in the turbo decoding algorithm. In this work, two novel approaches are investigated to reduce the memory usage in turbo decoding: (1) α-inverse matrix calculation, and (2) proper quantization of α and β values.

articleTitle: A comparison of multipath-dispersion-related microcellular mobile radio channel characteristics at 1.9 GHz and 5.8 GHz
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: There is considerable interest in determining differences between radio channel characteristics in the currently allocated mobile radio frequency bands and bands that might be allocated for this purpose in the future. This paper is therefore devoted to a determination and comparison of channel characteristics caused by multipath (time) dispersion on microcellular mobile radio channels at frequencies near 1.9 GHz and 5.8°GHz. Channel parameters that are considered include multipath spreads and various measures thereof, and frequency correlation characteristics.

articleTitle: Active array for s-band satellite communications
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: User Radio Access Equipment (URAE) having omnidirectional antennas will support only low data rates due to limitations on available power in both the up and down links. In order to support higher data rates — up to 64 kbps — URAE having medium gain antennas are envisaged. These higher gain antennas would provide a minimum G/T of −20dB/K over the coverage region along with an EIRP of 10dBW. With very low losses and state-of-the-art LNA performance this G/T corresponds to an edge of coverage directive gain of 4dBic.

articleTitle: Architectural study of active membrane antennas
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: One method to dramatically reduce the weight, volume and associated cost of space-based Synthetic Aperture Radars (SAR) is to replace the conventional rigid manifold antenna architecture with a flexible thin-film membrane. This has been successfully demonstrated as a passive array. To further reduce the cost and weight and provide 2D scanning required by space-based applications we also need to integrate the Transmit/Receive (T/R) function into the inflatable antenna elements. This paper explores the constraints that must be placed on the active electronics of a flexible antenna array and preliminary work in this area.

articleTitle: Analysis of varactor tuned active microstrip patch antenna
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The theoretical analysis of varactor tuned active microstrip antenna is proposed. The active antenna shows a marked improvement in tuning range, beamwidth and bandwidth. The proposed method predicts bandwidth of 35.5256%, which is higher than the earlier reported data.

articleTitle: Applications of projection method for beam shaping in reflectarray antennas
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: In this paper, beam shaping in reflectarray antennas based on the projection method is studied in detail. Individual elements of the array can be designed to control the phase distribution on the surface of a reflectarray antenna to realize a desired radiation pattern. A beam splitter based on this method has been designed and tested.

articleTitle: Direct far-field reconstruction from data measured by a cylindrical scanning facility
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: For electrically large antenna systems it is impossible or unpractical to measure directly the radiation patterns on a conventional far-field (FF) range. Therefore, for such antennas, it is useful to exploit near-field (NF) measurements to recover the FF patterns via NF-FF transformation techniques [1]. It is useful to note that NF measurements may be performed in a controlled environment, as an indoor shielded anechoic chamber, which allows to overcome those drawbacks that, due to weather conditions (rain, snow, etc.), electromagnetic (EM) interference, pollution and other, cannot be eliminated in FF outdoor measurements. In addition, NF scanning techniques represent the better choice when complete pattern and polarization measurements are required. Moreover, they provide the necessary information to determine the radiating field at the surface of the antenna (microwave holographic diagnostics). Among the NF-FF transformation techniques, the cylindrical scanning (Fig. 1) has attracted considerable attention [2-5]. At the cost of a moderate increase in the analytical and computational complication with respect to the planar scannings, it allows one to reconstruct, from a single set of NF measurements, the antenna complete radiation pattern save for the zones surrounding the spherical polar angles. By exploiting the analytical properties of EM fields [6], sampling expansions have been successfully applied to the NF-FF transformation with cylindrical scanning [3]. Unlike the approach in [2], the number of data on each ring decreases moving from the central measurement rings to the peripheral ones, and the linear spacing between the rings grows when the cylinder radius increases. However, such an approach still exhibits the shortcoming that the overall number of samples becomes unbounded when the height of the scanning cylinder approaches infinity. A new NF-FF transformation from a nonredundant number of data, which stays finite also for an unbounded cylinder, has been developed in [4] by assuming the antenna under test (AUT) as enclosed in a sphere (spherical modelling). Unfortunately, for elongated antennas, the spherical modelling gives rise to an useless increase in the number of NF data. Moreover, it prevents the possibility of considering measurement cylinders with a diameter smaller than the source height. A NF-FF transformation, which overcomes these drawbacks and reduces significantly the number of required data in the case of elongated antennas, has been proposed in [5], by applying the recent theoretical results concerning the nonredundant sampling representation of the EM field [7] and considering the antenna as enclosed in the smallest surface formed by a cylinder ended in two half-spheres. Since in [3-5] the case of an ideal probe has been considered, the effects of the measurement probe have not been taken into account in the evaluation of the antenna FF pattern.

articleTitle: Microwave and millimetre wave payloads for the measurement of the Cosmic Microwave Background
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The retrieval of a highly accurate map of the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) radiation is the scientific core of the Planck mission of the European Space Agency (ESA). The satellite will perform two complete sky surveys from its orbit around the L2 Lagrange point. The cryogenic-cooled receivers of the two instruments will measure in 10 frequency bands the microwave emission spectrum from 24 to 1000 GHz with unprecedented accuracy. The instruments are located at the focal plane of an off-axis double reflector of 1500mm projected aperture. Taken together, this assembly is an electrically large antenna varying from 120λ, to 5000λ with the operating frequencies. This paper presents the Planck microwave and millimetre wave instruments and reflectors and the expected RF performance.

articleTitle: A PNM implementation for large phased arrays
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Unlike quasi-optical techniques such as the Geometrical Theory of Diffraction (GTD), the Method of Moment (MoM) provides accurate and essential surface current information. For the electromagnetic scattering analysis of electrically large, perfectly electric conductor (PEC) bodies, several fast and efficient “Decompose-Solve-Recompose” (DSR) schemes are available in the literature. Among these, the Progressive Numerical Method (PNM) is a scatterer sectioning method that accounts for the progressive effect of previously computed surface current solutions [1]. In these scatterer decomposition techniques, coupling effects from adjacent subregions are included into the computation of each subregion. Typically, such techniques are especially suitable for very large scatterers since their solution accuracies improve with larger body sizes and are insensitive to their subregion sizes [2].

articleTitle: FEM CAD for the analysis and design of frequency selective surfaces
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The analysis and design of frequency selective surfaces (FSS) using commercial full wave finite element method (FEM) packages will be presented. Grating lobes phenomena can be easily visualised through the animated field option. The design and development of an improved FSS model using this commercial CAD package is presented and compared.

articleTitle: Small antenna measurement on ground reflection range
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: This paper presents the idea of measuring small antennas, in particular portable radio antenna using common 3 m and 10 m open area test site intended for EMC radiated measurements. This method involves the use of antenna modeling software to compare the free space radiation pattern and the ground reflection pattern of the calibrated standard reference antenna, and the antenna under test. From the patterns, the relationship between the known free space gains of the antenna and the ground reflection pattern is established. This information was later used to predict the positions to place the sensing antenna on the open area test site to pick up the appropriate peaks of the received amplitudes. By scanning the receiving antenna over the heights predicted, the free space gain of the antenna is then predicted using the relationship established earlier between the free space and ground reflection patterns. This paper recommends that portable antennas are should be measured in the horizontal position on the ground reflection range for better accuracy. The actual, measured data verifying the method is also presented.

articleTitle: Modal approach to the design of probe-fed cavity-backed patch arrays
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The modal analysis method of a probe-fed, cavity-backed patch element in a unit cell is presented. This type of element is considered for use in an electronically scanned horizontally polarized X-band aperture operating from 9.7 GHz to 10.3 GHz and with an azimuth scan of ±45°. The scanned characteristics of the element are found to be well suited for the intended application.

articleTitle: The RADARSAT-2&3 interferometric mission
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The Canadian Space Agency and MacDonald Dettwiler Associates (MDA) have just completed a definition study for the proposed RADARSAT-2/3 tandem interferometric mission. The objective of the mission is to provide a global Digital Elevation Model of the Earth compliant to US National Imaging and Mapping Agency (NIMA) Digital Terrain Elevation Data Level 3 (DTED-3) specification. The main requirements are to achieve a global accuracy better than 10 m (at 90% confidence level), relative accuracy of 2.0 m and 10 m nominal post-spacing. The paper gives an overview of the tandem mission, and presents a summary of technical investigations carried out by MDA on the mode of operation, the performance assessment, the orbit definition and the interferometric processing.

articleTitle: Study of millimetre-wave cell area coverage using weather radar data
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Cell area coverage in mm-wave fixed cellular systems was studied by considering the joint impact of rain attenuation and lognormal shadowing loss. Spatial information of rain attenuation was obtained from weather radar images, upon which radio cells were simulated. Coverage was computed by adding the distance-dependent mean and lognormal excess path losses to rain attenuation and integrating probability density of coverage over the entire cell area given the power margin at the cell perimeter. Statistical results for a region near Montreal are presented.

articleTitle: Ka band MMICs in GaAs technology
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: This paper presents some recent results obtained on a new implementation of a Monolithic Microwave Integrated Circuit (MMIC) six-port junction related to a hardware type receiver designed for QPSK communications [1], [2]. This junction is the basis of a direct conversion wide band six-port millimeter wave receiver. This new hardware receiver is proposed as a robust, rugged, low cost receiver for use in wide band wireless mass market QPSK communications [3]-[5]. LMDS services are a prime example of communication equipment needing such receivers.

articleTitle: Fields of a cell phone with a hands-free kit adapter
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: This paper examines the electric field inside a simple model of the human head, due to a cellular telephone with a “hands-free kit” (HFK) adapter. The cell phone is a metal box with a quarter-wave monopole on the top. The HFK wire is connected to the bottom of the handset and runs up parallel to the body to a point near the location of the ear. The body, neck and head are represented with box models, including layers for the skin, muscle, and bone in the head, which is filled with brain material. The fields due to the handset, monopole, HFK wire and head, neck and torso are found with the finite-difference time-domain method. The fields in the head due to the handset alone are the reference case. When the handset and HFK are operated in free space the fields in the region where the head would be are found to be stronger than those of the handset alone. When the body is present, the fields near the surface of the head with the HFK depend strongly on the spacing of the HFK wire to the body. However, for the two cases examined, the field strength in the brain with the HFK wire is always smaller than the field strength of the handset alone.

articleTitle: The effect of stacked U-slot patch on the radiation parameters of rectangular U-slot microstrip antenna
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The single layer U-slot rectangular patch antenna has been found to provide impedance bandwidth of about 30% [1]. A bandwidth of up to 40% is obtained with a U-slot patch antenna stacked with a parasitic patch [2]. In this paper the effect of second U-slot stacked with the same geometry is presented, Fig. 1. A bandwidth as high as 46% is obtained.

articleTitle: Adaptation of lcmv-based beamforming by vector space projection
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Over the last few years the demand for wireless communication services has been risen beyond expectations. The operation of wireless communication is subject to limited available spectrum, thus, how to improve frequency reuse efficiency is important. Spatial division multiple access (SDMA) scheme is another mean, besides that of TDMA, FDMA and CDMA, to expand channel capacity to meet the escalating demand of wireless communication services. To achieve the scheme of SDMA, one should introduce array systems to explore space resource, which stimulates the development of smart antenna systems (SAS) for new generation wireless communication systems [1-4].

articleTitle: Impact of adaptive antenna systems on spectrum management
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: This paper addresses the impact of adaptive antenna systems on interference mitigation as well as on improvements to communication distance, system capacity and spectrum utilization in terrestrial mobile systems.

articleTitle: Major technological innovations introduced in the large antennas of The Deep Space Network
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The NASA Deep Space Network (DSN) is the largest and most sensitive scientific, telecommunications and radio navigation network in the world. Its principal responsibilities are to provide communications, tracking, and science services to most of the world's spacecraft that travel beyond low Earth orbit. The network consists of three Deep Space Communications Complexes which are located on three continents: at Goldstone in Southern California's Mojave Desert; near Madrid Spain; and near Canberra Australia. Each of the three complexes consists of multiple large antennas equipped with ultra sensitive receiving systems. A centralized Signal Processing Center (SPC) remotely controls the antennas, generates and transmits spacecraft commands, and receives and processes the spacecraft telemetry.

articleTitle: Multi-band antenna for mobile communication standards
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Nowadays numerous standards in mobile phones and short range links are emerging. The development of antennas covering all those allowed frequencies with only one element and one feeding appears to be an important goal [1]. For example, base stations for mobiles are mostly composed of different arrays of antennas, each array working for only one band. The purpose of the presented study is to develop a single antenna which can be able to offer good performances for all GSM, DCS, UMTS and also Bluetooth bands. This antenna was designed and optimised using FDTD tools, and measurements results of a prototype are detailed. Moreover a four elements square array is described. Higher gain is achieved with a conical radiation pattern, and the beam steering ability of such an array is discussed.

articleTitle: Performance of pcs with antenna diversity in sub-Rayleigh fading
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Nakagami fading channels have been used as a very flexible, and fairly accurate approximation of realistic fading in wireless systems [1-3]. In particular, sub-Rayleigh fading, i.e. fading with severity parameter 0.5 ≤ m ≤ 1, describes situation where only a few major scatterers contribute to the signal in the antenna of the receiver, and there is no Line of Sight (LOS) present. Due to a finite spatial correlation of the incident electromagnetic field, and the movement of the vehicle, the fading process possesses certain correlation properties [13], which must be accurately represented when numerical simulation of wireless systems is considered. There are very few algorithms which allow such accurate modelling [3-5]. Most of these algorithm are either based on some numerical evaluation of the parameters of the model [4], or provide an approximation for the resulting correlation function with a fixed uncontrollable error [5]. As a result these models have limiting application in laborious Monte Carlo simulation of the wireless systems. In this paper we suggest a model which allows complete analytical description of the marginal probability density function (PDF) of the envelope and its correlation function. At the same time it provides for an accurate numerical simulation algorithm along with the possibility to derive probability density of any order. In contrast to [4], we provide analytically tractable algorithms which allows the model parameters to be found in closed form. At the same time we avoid the complications related to the representation of a correlation function as a product of two correlation functions [4]. As an example we consider application of the simulation technique suggested to a system with antenna diversity.

articleTitle: Discrete time domain images for sommerfeld half-space problem with vertical magnetic dipole based on transient spectral domain method
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: The optimization rule is applied to evaluate the transient fields due to a Sommerfeld half-space problem of a vertical Magnetic Dipole. The Transient Spectral Domain Method (TSDM) is used for theoretical formulatation of the problem. The numerical example is given for the magnetic vector potential leads to a discrete time domain image representation of the Sommerfeld half-space problem.

articleTitle: Accurate CAD formulas of passive components in integrated circuits, from a bootstrapped fuzzy EM series
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: Started with a physics-based fuzzy formulation, the Fuzzy EM does a rigorous derivation, built-in with one or two arbitrary constants, and leads to an accurate CAD formula of a practical circuit component. Bootstrapping means that the CAD formula resulted is in turn taken as fuzzy formulation leading to the CAD formula of a more complicated component. In succession, a bootstrapping series is formed giving the field theoretic formulas of many of the passive components of an integrated circuit. The components in this paper are the fundamental overlaid capacitor C, the effect perforated ground for multiplayer circuit, the spiral inductor L and the resistor R under all frequencies, from DC to RF. Because of the “mid-course correction” of one arbitrary constant in each step, the accuracies of the formulas are maintained at around 2%.

articleTitle: Smart antenna arrays — A geometrical explanation of how they work
publicationTitle: 2002 9th International Symposium on Antenna Technology and Applied Electromagnetics
abstract: For fixed bandwidth and total radiated power, with Rayleigh fading, a wireless system with multiple antennas at both transmitter and receiver has a channel capacity which grows linearly (rather than logarithmically) with the number of antennas. This result, which assumes separate information is sent out of each transmit antenna, holds true even though the transmitter does not know the complex channel transfer characteristic. By explicitly spreading out the antennas well beyond a wavelength, we show that such capacities can be achieved not only on Rayleigh channels with many scatterers, but also on deterministic channels with direct line-of-sight (LOS) paths only and no scatterers. Roughly speaking, the wide spacing, replicates the effect of scatterers which create images and thus serves to spread out the apparent source of the signals over a wider angular range. In this way capacities on the order of C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">lin</inf> = nlog<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>(1 + ρ) bps/Hz can be obtained for LOS as well as Rayleigh channels when n transmit and n receive antennas are used. In contrast, when the transmit antennas are closely spaced, the number of degrees of freedom on a LOS channel degenerate, resulting in capacities of only C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">log</inf> = log<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>(1 + nρ).
